title: Abrahamic inheritance, chosen people and rival continuities
scope: A linked atlas of every tradition already represented in the comparative-religion directory plus additional Abrahamic, restorationist and Israelite-identification movements discussed in the Theology Wiki. Inclusion does not mean every group claims to be the chosen people. Claim types distinguish direct Israelite continuity, covenantal inheritance, restoration, progressive revelation, genealogical relationship and non-Abrahamic comparison.

groups.name: African Hebrew Israelites of Jerusalem
groups.continuity_claim: The African Hebrew Israelites of Jerusalem developed a specific Israelite identity, migration and communal-restoration narrative within the wider Black Hebrew Israelite field.
groups.scope_note: Their claims should be studied as the claims of this particular movement rather than generalized to Black Jews or all Hebrew Israelites.
groups.summary: The African Hebrew Israelites of Jerusalem developed a specific Israelite identity, migration and communal-restoration narrative within the wider Black Hebrew Israelite field.

groups.name: Ahmadiyya Muslim traditions
groups.claim_type: Islamic Abrahamic restoration with later messianic claim
groups.continuity_claim: Ahmadiyya identifies as Muslim and therefore inherits Islam's Abrahamic restoration claim while adding distinctive claims concerning Mirza Ghulam Ahmad.
groups.scope_note: Its Muslim self-identification and other Muslim authorities' disagreements should both be represented without the Wiki deciding a reader's faith.
groups.summary: The community traces its foundation to Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in Qadian in 1889, in British India. Its prophetic and messianic claims and its Muslim self-identification need to be distinguished from other authorities' assessments.

groups.name: Alawite / Nusayri traditions
groups.claim_type: Abrahamic genealogy but not a simple chosen-people claim
groups.continuity_claim: Alawite or Nusayri traditions developed in an Islamic setting and remain part of the broader Abrahamic religious history while preserving distinctive teachings and communal identity.
groups.scope_note: Restricted or disputed teachings should not be invented from outsider analogies.
groups.summary: Friedman's study supplies a scholarly point of entry. Only publication and chapter metadata were available here; this record is not a completed account of restricted doctrines or every adherent's identity.

groups.name: Anusim, conversos and crypto-Jewish histories
groups.continuity_claim: Anusim, converso and crypto-Jewish histories concern people forced into other public identities while Jewish ancestry or practices could persist.
groups.scope_note: This is a history of coercion, continuity and descendants, not one denomination with a single present-day doctrine.
groups.summary: Forced conversion, covert observance and later descendants concern historical circumstances and diverse identities, not one uniformly constituted denomination. Present identity must not be assigned from ancestry alone.

groups.name: Assyrian Church of the East and Chaldean Catholic Church
groups.continuity_claim: The Assyrian Church of the East and Chaldean Catholic Church both inherit the biblical Abraham-Israel-Christ narrative through East Syriac Christianity.
groups.scope_note: They require separate ecclesial histories even where language, liturgy and regional heritage overlap.
groups.summary: These require distinct church entries despite related East Syriac heritage. Neither the name Assyrian nor a historical label such as Nestorian constitutes a claim that the church is Gnostic.

groups.name: Baha'i Faith
groups.continuity_claim: The Baha'i Faith places Abraham within a progressive history of divine revelation that continues through later Manifestations of God.
groups.scope_note: This universalizes inheritance rather than claiming that one ethnic community alone replaces Israel.
groups.summary: The community names Buddha and Zoroaster within progressive revelation, alongside other divine educators. This is its theology of religious relationship, not evidence that all earlier figures taught one identical system.

groups.name: Basilides and Basilidian testimony
groups.continuity_claim: Basilidian traditions belong to the contested early-Christian field and are relevant as rival claims about authentic revelation.
groups.scope_note: Most surviving descriptions come through opponents, so a confident reconstruction of their Abrahamic self-understanding requires source recovery.
groups.summary: Irenaeus I.24 reports a system associated with Basilides, but it remains an opponent's account. It cannot serve as an unquestioned transcript of all Basilidian belief and conduct.

groups.name: Beta Israel
groups.continuity_claim: Beta Israel belongs to the history of Jewish and Israelite identity in Ethiopia and later Israel.
groups.scope_note: Its history should be studied through its own textual and communal witnesses rather than reduced to one lost-tribe legend.
groups.summary: ANU Museum's Orit exhibit documents a named sacred scroll, eight-book contents and custodial history. It supplies a concrete starting point rather than a story of an unchanging community completely isolated for a fixed millennium.

groups.name: Black Hebrew Israelite movements
groups.continuity_claim: A diverse field of Black Hebrew Israelite movements identifies particular African-descended peoples with biblical Israel or the lost tribes.
groups.scope_note: This is not one denomination, and ancestry claims, racial teachings and relations with Judaism differ sharply among groups.
groups.summary: A diverse field of Black Hebrew Israelite movements identifies particular African-descended peoples with biblical Israel or the lost tribes.

groups.name: British Israelism / Anglo-Israelism
groups.continuity_claim: British-Israelite movements claim that British or related peoples descend from the lost tribes of Israel and therefore inherit biblical promises.
groups.scope_note: Genealogical assertion, theological use and historical evidence are separate questions; the page is an orientation stub pending dedicated source work.
groups.summary: British-Israelite movements claim that British or related peoples descend from the lost tribes of Israel and therefore inherit biblical promises.

groups.name: Buddhist traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Buddhist traditions enter the Wiki through Manichaean, Baha'i, Ahmadiyya and comparative-esotericism discussions rather than through an Abrahamic covenant claim.
groups.scope_note: They are a control case showing that universal prophetic systems can incorporate non-Abrahamic teachers.
groups.summary: The nonself discourse supplies a precise comparison with a substantial liberated light-soul. Shared ascetic vocabulary does not establish an identical account of personhood.

groups.name: Catholic Christianity
groups.continuity_claim: Catholic Christianity places the Church within Abrahamic and Israelite salvation history through Christ while contemporary Catholic teaching also rejects portraying Jews as simply rejected or cursed by God.
groups.scope_note: This page should distinguish participation in Abraham's call from crude replacement formulas.
groups.summary: Catholic Christianity places the Church within Abrahamic and Israelite salvation history through Christ while contemporary Catholic teaching also rejects portraying Jews as simply rejected or cursed by God.

groups.name: Christian Identity
groups.continuity_claim: Christian Identity developed from British-Israelite ideas into explicitly racialized interpretations of biblical Israel and chosenness.
groups.scope_note: Its racist and antisemitic doctrines must be described as features of that movement rather than attributed to ordinary Christianity, Judaism or British-Israelism as a whole.
groups.summary: Christian Identity developed from British-Israelite ideas into explicitly racialized interpretations of biblical Israel and chosenness.

groups.name: Christianity generally
groups.continuity_claim: Christianity broadly reads the Abrahamic promise through Christ; Galatians 3 is a classic formulation in which those who belong to Christ are called Abraham's offspring and heirs according to promise.
groups.scope_note: Christian traditions disagree sharply about Israel, the Church, supersession, covenant and the continuing role of the Jewish people.
groups.summary: Christianity broadly reads the Abrahamic promise through Christ; Galatians 3 is a classic formulation in which those who belong to Christ are called Abraham's offspring and heirs according to promise.

groups.name: Conservative Judaism
groups.continuity_claim: Conservative Judaism understands Jewish covenantal peoplehood as continuous while combining commitment to halakhic tradition with historical development and institutional interpretation.
groups.scope_note: This page is an orientation stub pending dedicated movement sources.
groups.summary: Conservative Judaism understands Jewish covenantal peoplehood as continuous while combining commitment to halakhic tradition with historical development and institutional interpretation.

groups.name: Coptic Orthodox and Coptic Catholic churches
groups.continuity_claim: Coptic Orthodox and Coptic Catholic Christians participate in the Christian claim that the Abrahamic promises reach their fulfillment through Christ.
groups.scope_note: The two churches are distinct institutions and should not be conflated simply because both are Egyptian.
groups.summary: Distinguish the Coptic Orthodox Church from the Coptic Catholic Church. The 1973 Orthodox-Catholic declaration affirms Trinity and real humanity and divinity, not an anti-incarnational Gnostic creed.

groups.name: Druze tradition
groups.claim_type: Abrahamic genealogy but not a simple chosen-people claim
groups.continuity_claim: The Druze tradition developed historically from an Ismaili environment and therefore belongs in the wider Abrahamic genealogy while developing a distinct religious identity.
groups.scope_note: It should not be forced into the formula 'we are the true Israel' unless a specific source makes that claim.
groups.summary: The Institute of Ismaili Studies lecture description locates formative developments in an eleventh-century Fatimid setting while examining a distinctive tradition. It does not authenticate the supplied list of secret sages.

groups.name: Early Jewish Jesus movement
groups.continuity_claim: The earliest Jesus movement emerged within Jewish life and initially presented claims about Messiah, Israel and covenant before Christianity became a predominantly non-Jewish religion.
groups.scope_note: This page distinguishes an internal Jewish messianic claim from later Christian theories of covenantal inheritance.
groups.summary: The earliest Jesus movement emerged within Jewish life and initially presented claims about Messiah, Israel and covenant before Christianity became a predominantly non-Jewish religion.

groups.name: Eastern Orthodox Christianity
groups.continuity_claim: Eastern Orthodox Christianity understands the Church within the biblical history of Abraham, Israel, covenant and fulfillment in Christ.
groups.scope_note: The many autocephalous churches share communion and tradition without becoming one centralized administrative institution.
groups.summary: Eastern Orthodox Christianity understands the Church within the biblical history of Abraham, Israel, covenant and fulfillment in Christ.

groups.name: Ebionites and related Jewish-Christian traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Where reconstructable, Ebionite traditions represent attempts to combine Jesus as Messiah with continued Torah-observant Jewish identity.
groups.scope_note: Most evidence is late and often comes through opponents, so this page remains a source-recovery prospect.
groups.summary: Where reconstructable, Ebionite traditions represent attempts to combine Jesus as Messiah with continued Torah-observant Jewish identity.

groups.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Christianity
groups.claim_type: Christian heirs of Abraham with strong Israelite symbolism
groups.continuity_claim: Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity participates in Christian Abrahamic inheritance while giving unusually prominent roles to Zion, the Ark, Solomon and the Queen of Sheba traditions.
groups.scope_note: Traditional sacred history, liturgy and independently established chronology should remain distinct.
groups.summary: Ethiopian Orthodox Christianity participates in Christian Abrahamic inheritance while giving unusually prominent roles to Zion, the Ark, Solomon and the Queen of Sheba traditions.

groups.name: Greek Orthodox and Melkite Greek Catholic traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Greek Orthodox and Melkite Greek Catholic traditions both inhabit the Christian Abrahamic narrative while belonging to different ecclesial communions.
groups.scope_note: Their shared Byzantine heritage does not erase their institutional differences.
groups.summary: Shared Byzantine liturgical heritage does not erase distinct ecclesial communion. Greek Orthodox and Melkite Catholic labels should not be used as interchangeable names for one institution.

groups.name: Hasidic Judaism
groups.continuity_claim: Hasidic Judaism operates within Orthodox Jewish peoplehood and covenant while emphasizing distinctive devotional, mystical and communal forms around Torah, prayer and the tzaddik or rebbe.
groups.scope_note: Hasidic groups are not one centralized denomination and should not be assigned one attitude toward Christianity.
groups.summary: Hasidic Judaism operates within Orthodox Jewish peoplehood and covenant while emphasizing distinctive devotional, mystical and communal forms around Torah, prayer and the tzaddik or rebbe.

groups.name: Hebrew Roots movements
groups.continuity_claim: Hebrew Roots movements urge Christians to recover Torah, Hebrew names, biblical feasts or other perceived Israelite foundations of faith.
groups.scope_note: Claims range from cultural or theological restoration to stronger assertions about Israelite identity, so individual organizations require separate sourcing.
groups.summary: Hebrew Roots movements urge Christians to recover Torah, Hebrew names, biblical feasts or other perceived Israelite foundations of faith.

groups.name: Hermetic texts
groups.continuity_claim: Hermetic writings are central to the Wiki's esoteric comparisons but do not form an Abrahamic chosen-people claim.
groups.scope_note: They remain in the atlas because the user asked that traditions already discussed in the Wiki not disappear from the map.
groups.summary: Hermetic works in Nag Hammadi Codex VI include a prayer joining knowledge, embodied transformation and a shared meal. Physical collection with other writings does not imply identical doctrine.

groups.name: Ibadism
groups.continuity_claim: Ibadism is an early and distinct Muslim tradition and therefore participates in Islam's claim to Abrahamic continuity.
groups.scope_note: Its separate legal and historical development should not be reduced to a midpoint between Sunni and Shia.
groups.summary: Wilkinson's study describes a distinctive early school and the importance of Basran, Omani and North African histories. The chapter abstracts do not support treating every period as uniformly peaceful, democratic or unchanged.

groups.name: Islam generally
groups.continuity_claim: Islam presents Abraham as a primordial submitter to God and situates Muhammad's message as restoration and continuation of that monotheistic path.
groups.scope_note: This broad claim should not erase Sunni, Shia, Ibadi, Ahmadiyya and other differences.
groups.summary: Islam presents Abraham as a primordial submitter to God and situates Muhammad's message as restoration and continuation of that monotheistic path.

groups.name: Ismaili traditions
groups.claim_type: Islamic Abrahamic restoration / living sacred authority
groups.continuity_claim: Ismaili traditions participate in Islam's Abrahamic continuity while giving the Imam a distinctive role in authoritative interpretation.
groups.scope_note: Different Ismaili branches require their own historical treatment.
groups.summary: The cited institutional account emphasizes interpretation and imamship from a Nizari setting. Its perspective is not automatically a description of all Ismaili branches, and esoteric interpretation is not proof of one Gnostic ancestry.

groups.name: Jehovah's Witnesses
groups.continuity_claim: Jehovah's Witnesses interpret Abraham's promised seed through Christ and a distinct understanding of spiritual Israel.
groups.scope_note: Their claim is theological rather than an assertion that all members are literal descendants of ancient Israel.
groups.summary: The cited official account rejects the Trinity and describes Jesus as a created Son. Nontrinitarian belief alone does not establish identity with a Jewish, Islamic or ancient Gnostic doctrine.

groups.name: Kabbalah
groups.continuity_claim: Kabbalistic traditions interpret Torah, creation, divine life and repair from within Jewish covenantal identity rather than constituting a new ethnic Israel.
groups.scope_note: Different Kabbalistic schools and periods should be separated rather than turned into one timeless cosmology.
groups.summary: Kabbalistic traditions interpret Torah, creation, divine life and repair from within Jewish covenantal identity rather than constituting a new ethnic Israel.

groups.name: Kabbalah and Hasidic traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Kabbalistic and Hasidic traditions operate within Jewish covenantal identity while offering distinctive mystical interpretations of divine life, Torah and the role of the righteous.
groups.scope_note: They do not constitute a separate ethnic Israel from Judaism; their continuity claim is nested inside Jewish peoplehood and covenant.
groups.summary: Tanya supplies one account of divine vitality, the other side and repentance. It is not evidence that all Jewish mystics share one cosmology or now accept Christian doctrines.

groups.name: Karaite Judaism
groups.continuity_claim: Karaite Judaism claims Jewish and Israelite continuity while rejecting rabbinic Oral Law as binding authority.
groups.scope_note: Its disagreement is over the authoritative form of interpretation, not a rejection of Abrahamic-Israelite identity.
groups.summary: Rejection of rabbinic Oral Law as binding does not entail the absence of commentary, legal interpretation or inherited practice. The community's own reading-room catalogue demonstrates those genres.

groups.name: Latter-day Saints
groups.continuity_claim: Latter-day Saint teaching gives the Abrahamic covenant and the gathering of Israel a prominent role, with participation understood through descent, adoption and covenant.
groups.scope_note: This is a particularly explicit restorationist form of Israel language within Christianity.
groups.summary: The church's own introduction affirms additional scripture and a Godhead account distinct from Nicene consubstantiality. Those claims should be represented in their own terms rather than called a surviving ancient Gnostic sect.

groups.name: Mandaeans
groups.claim_type: Abrahamic genealogy but not an Abrahamic inheritance claim
groups.continuity_claim: Mandaeans share a scriptural and historical environment with Jewish, Christian and Baptist figures while preserving a strongly distinct religious identity.
groups.scope_note: Their tradition is not accurately summarized as 'we are the true heirs of Abraham'; Abraham and several other Abrahamic figures can be treated critically.
groups.summary: A living tradition with distinctive scriptures, rites and community self-understanding. Its Book of John is not a canonical Christian Gospel, and Miriai's narrative requires its own textual treatment.

groups.name: Manichaeism
groups.continuity_claim: Manichaeism places Jesus within a wider prophetic history that also incorporates figures such as Buddha and Zoroaster, with Mani presenting a culminating revelation.
groups.scope_note: This is a successor-revelation claim, not an ethnic claim to be Israel.
groups.summary: The two principles, rescue of light and distinct community obligations need to be studied together. Invoking Jesus, Buddha and Zoroaster does not make their teachings interchangeable.

groups.name: Marcion and Marcionite traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Marcionite Christianity claimed the authentic gospel of Christ while sharply separating that revelation from the creator and law associated with Israel.
groups.scope_note: It is therefore a major boundary case: historically Christian and biblical, but not a simple claim to continue Israel's covenant.
groups.summary: The tradition belongs in questions about scripture, law and the relation between creator and redeemer. It should not be equated automatically with every Sethian or Valentinian position.

groups.name: Maronite Catholic Church
groups.continuity_claim: The Maronite Catholic Church participates in the Christian and Catholic reading of Abrahamic salvation history while preserving an Eastern Syriac heritage.
groups.scope_note: Communion with Rome does not make the Maronite tradition identical to the Latin rite.
groups.summary: An Eastern Catholic church with its own tradition; communion with Rome does not mean every Catholic uses the Latin rite. An Eastern liturgy is not evidence of Gnostic cosmology.

groups.name: Messianic Judaism
groups.claim_type: Jewish covenant continuity plus Christian messianic fulfillment
groups.continuity_claim: Messianic Jewish movements seek to retain Jewish or Israelite covenantal identity while confessing Jesus or Yeshua as Messiah.
groups.scope_note: The field contains disputes over Jewish status, Torah practice, church relations and institutional definition; one movement should not stand for all.
groups.summary: Messianic Jewish movements seek to retain Jewish or Israelite covenantal identity while confessing Jesus or Yeshua as Messiah.

groups.name: Nation of Islam
groups.continuity_claim: The Nation of Islam emerged in an Islamic and biblical vocabulary but has distinctive teachings that separate it from mainstream Sunni and Shia Islam.
groups.scope_note: Its Abrahamic relationship is genealogical and interpretive rather than a simple continuation claim identical to mainstream Islam.
groups.summary: A named community source identifies its connection with Elijah Muhammad's teaching. A complete account must distinguish the movement's own claims, later organizational histories and other African American Muslim communities.

groups.name: Old Calendarist and True Orthodox jurisdictions
groups.continuity_claim: Old Calendarist and True Orthodox jurisdictions understand themselves within Orthodox Christian continuity and therefore within Christian Abrahamic salvation history.
groups.scope_note: Calendar disputes and jurisdictional claims do not, by themselves, define an independent Abrahamic people.
groups.summary: A separate history of particular calendar controversies and jurisdictions is needed. Calendar usage alone should not be used to infer a church's communion status, esotericism or entire doctrine.

groups.name: Oriental Orthodox Christianity
groups.continuity_claim: Oriental Orthodox churches understand themselves within the Abraham-Israel-Christ story while preserving distinct ancient church traditions.
groups.scope_note: Coptic, Armenian, Syriac, Ethiopian, Eritrean and Malankara histories should not be collapsed into one ethnic or liturgical identity.
groups.summary: Oriental Orthodox churches understand themselves within the Abraham-Israel-Christ story while preserving distinct ancient church traditions.

groups.name: Orthodox Judaism
groups.continuity_claim: Orthodox Judaism understands Jews as continuing the covenantal people of Israel and gives binding authority to Torah as interpreted through rabbinic tradition.
groups.scope_note: Orthodox Judaism itself contains substantial internal diversity and should not be represented by one rabbi or one philosophical school.
groups.summary: Orthodox Judaism understands Jews as continuing the covenantal people of Israel and gives binding authority to Torah as interpreted through rabbinic tradition.

groups.name: Protestant Christianity
groups.continuity_claim: Protestant churches generally inherit the Christian claim that faith in Christ brings participation in Abraham's promise.
groups.scope_note: Views of Israel, covenant, law, baptism, election and church identity differ widely across Protestant traditions.
groups.summary: Protestant churches generally inherit the Christian claim that faith in Christ brings participation in Abraham's promise.

groups.name: Qumran texts and Essene comparisons
groups.continuity_claim: The sectarian Qumran texts portray a faithful covenant community within Israel rather than a later non-Israelite heir to Abraham.
groups.scope_note: This is a historical remnant claim reconstructed from particular texts, not a living denomination or proof that every Dead Sea Scroll was produced by one group.
groups.summary: The Dead Sea Scrolls contain multiple works and forms of community organization. Particular sectarian texts can be compared with reports about Essenes without making every manuscript the work of one monastic group.

groups.name: Rabbinic Judaism: Orthodox, Conservative and Reform
groups.continuity_claim: Rabbinic Judaism understands the Jewish people as continuing Israel's covenantal history through Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Torah and communal obligation.
groups.scope_note: Orthodox, Conservative and Reform Judaism require separate pages because they interpret covenant, law and election differently.
groups.summary: These labels should receive separate institutional and historical entries. This edition does not infer a uniform attitude to Jesus or mysticism from a single medieval author or modern declaration.

groups.name: Rastafari
groups.continuity_claim: Rastafari reworks biblical Israel, Babylon, Zion, Ethiopia and exile within African and diasporic history.
groups.scope_note: Different houses and teachers vary, so the page should not treat one Israelite identification as the entire tradition.
groups.summary: The museum and scholarly records connect Jamaican origins, scriptural reinterpretation and religious symbolism. Interpretations of Selassie and community practice require attention to diversity rather than one imposed creed.

groups.name: Reform Judaism
groups.continuity_claim: Reform Judaism retains Jewish covenantal identity while commonly interpreting chosenness in terms of mission, responsibility and ethical witness rather than superiority.
groups.scope_note: Specific platforms and congregations should be dated because Reform formulations have changed historically.
groups.summary: Reform Judaism retains Jewish covenantal identity while commonly interpreting chosenness in terms of mission, responsibility and ethical witness rather than superiority.

groups.name: Sacred Name movements
groups.continuity_claim: Sacred Name movements emphasize recovering the divine name and often other features understood as original Hebrew or Israelite worship.
groups.scope_note: The movement family is diverse; recovering a name is not by itself proof of ethnic descent or sole covenantal legitimacy.
groups.summary: Sacred Name movements emphasize recovering the divine name and often other features understood as original Hebrew or Israelite worship.

groups.name: Saint Thomas Christians
groups.continuity_claim: Saint Thomas Christian communities in India participate in Christian Abrahamic inheritance through several modern church communions.
groups.scope_note: The traditional apostolic origin and the later institutional histories need to be distinguished.
groups.summary: Kerala's Thomas Christian heritage now spans distinct church affiliations. Apostolic origins should be identified as a tradition rather than treated as a securely witnessed arrival date for every later community.

groups.name: Samaritans
groups.continuity_claim: Israelite Samaritans understand themselves as preserving ancient Israelite identity, Torah, priesthood and the sacred center at Mount Gerizim.
groups.scope_note: This is one of the clearest living claims to direct continuity with ancient Israel and competes with Jewish accounts on important points.
groups.summary: The Samaritan museum presents a distinctive five-book Torah and priestly heritage. The community is not adequately described merely as an unusual modern Jewish denomination.

groups.name: Sethian writings
groups.continuity_claim: Sethian writings reuse biblical figures and Jewish-Christian materials but do not straightforwardly claim to be the ethnic or covenantal Israel of Abraham.
groups.scope_note: Their importance here is genealogical and interpretive, not a simple chosen-people claim.
groups.summary: A scholarly grouping includes writings with distinctive divine genealogies and a lower ruler. A common classification does not establish one fixed institution or two independent primordial creators in every tractate.

groups.name: Seventh-day Adventists
groups.continuity_claim: Seventh-day Adventism understands itself within Christian Abrahamic inheritance and gives special theological importance to an end-time remnant and mission.
groups.scope_note: A remnant claim is not identical to a claim of biological descent from ancient Israel.
groups.summary: Seventh-day Adventism understands itself within Christian Abrahamic inheritance and gives special theological importance to an end-time remnant and mission.

groups.name: Shia Islam
groups.claim_type: Islamic Abrahamic restoration plus sacred lineage
groups.continuity_claim: Shia traditions share Islam's Abrahamic claim while emphasizing authority through the Prophet's family and the Imams in distinctive ways.
groups.scope_note: Twelver, Ismaili, Zaydi and other Shia traditions should not be collapsed into one doctrine of leadership.
groups.summary: Shia traditions share Islam's Abrahamic claim while emphasizing authority through the Prophet's family and the Imams in distinctive ways.

groups.name: Sufi traditions and orders
groups.claim_type: Inner lineage within Islamic Abrahamic continuity
groups.continuity_claim: Sufi orders and traditions generally operate within Muslim Abrahamic identity while emphasizing spiritual transmission, remembrance and disciplined paths of transformation.
groups.scope_note: Sufism is not normally a mutually exclusive third denomination beside Sunni and Shia.
groups.summary: Sufism describes devotional and interpretive streams and orders, not a mutually exclusive third denomination beside Sunni and Shia. Remembrance is one important practice, not the full identity of every order.

groups.name: Sunni and Shia traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Sunni and Shia traditions both understand Islam as the continuation and restoration of Abraham's submission to the one God, while differing over authority and leadership after Muhammad.
groups.scope_note: The aggregate page points to separate Sunni and Shia pages because the traditions are not one institutional body.
groups.summary: Shared commitments coexist with differing accounts of authority, law and interpretation. These broad labels contain internal schools and communities rather than two completely uniform sets of practice.

groups.name: Sunni Islam
groups.continuity_claim: Sunni Islam participates in the Quranic claim to Abrahamic continuity through Muhammad and the Muslim community.
groups.scope_note: Sunni schools differ in law, theology, devotional practice and political history; this page is an orientation entry, not one doctrinal profile.
groups.summary: Sunni Islam participates in the Quranic claim to Abrahamic continuity through Muhammad and the Muslim community.

groups.name: Valentinian traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Valentinian traditions claim Christian revelation while reinterpreting creation, salvation, scripture and spiritual identity through an esoteric cosmology.
groups.scope_note: This is a claim to authentic Christian knowledge, not a direct ethnic-Israel claim.
groups.summary: Ptolemy's intermediate just maker and Philip's ritual mysteries complicate the assumption that all esoteric Christians condemned the same evil creator and rejected all ritual.

groups.name: Yazidi tradition
groups.continuity_claim: Yazidi tradition is an important neighboring West Asian religion in the Wiki but is not accurately summarized as a claim to inherit Abraham's covenant.
groups.scope_note: Outsider accusations about its worship are not a substitute for community and scholarly sources.
groups.summary: Oral sacred transmission and the disputed status of commonly circulated printed holy books require particular care. Hostile outsider labels are not reliable descriptions of the community's worship.

groups.name: Zaydi Shia traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Zaydi Shia traditions participate in Islam's Abrahamic claim while developing a distinctive account of legitimate imamship.
groups.scope_note: The page should distinguish historical theology from contemporary political movements.
groups.summary: The movement associated with Zayd has distinctive accounts of imamship and a complex history. Describing it merely as the Shia group closest to Sunni Islam substitutes a single scale for that history.

groups.name: Zoroastrian traditions
groups.continuity_claim: Zoroastrian traditions are important to the Wiki's history of apocalyptic and dualistic ideas but do not derive their identity from Abraham's covenant.
groups.scope_note: They are included as a comparative neighbor, not as a claimant to Israelite chosenness.
groups.summary: The relationships among Ahura Mazda and opposing spirits vary across historical texts and interpretations. One equal-two-gods formula is not an adequate description of every period.
